opex.note: Building Photoshop, Acrobat, Firefly AI and the rest of the product line.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and marketing — Adobe's biggest running cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day: finance, legal, HR, offices.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions.

follow100Note: The split to notice: sales & marketing ($27.03) costs Adobe more per $100 than research & development ($19.05). Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
oneTimers: Adobe's non-GAAP profit of $2,424M (EPS $6.13) excludes $544M of stock-based and deferred compensation plus $58M of intangible amortization — the gap between the two profit figures is mostly paying employees in shares.
Adobe raised its full-year FY26 targets alongside this print: revenue of $26,576M–$26,626M and GAAP EPS of $18.12–$18.17.
otherDetail: Non-operating items netted to just $3M of income: $21M of investment gains and $48M of other income, almost fully offset by $66M of interest expense.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Creative Cloud, Acrobat and Experience Cloud subscriptions — 97 cents of every revenue dollar. Creative & Marketing Professionals paid $4,650M (+13%); Business Professionals & Consumers paid $1,910M (+16%).

segments.name: Product
segments.note: One-time software licenses — a small, shrinking legacy line from before Adobe moved to subscriptions.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Consulting, training and support services sold alongside the software.

takeaways.text: Revenue from Adobe's AI-first products grew more than 150% year over year, and the company passed 1 billion monthly active users across its creativity and productivity apps. The AI add-ons are becoming a real business, not a demo.
takeaways.title: AI is Adobe's growth engine now

takeaways.text: Total ARR — the annualized value of all subscriptions — ended the quarter at $27.50B, and remaining performance obligations (contracted future revenue) reached $22.16B. Very little of Adobe's revenue has to be re-won each quarter.
takeaways.title: The subscription machine keeps compounding

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 13% but net income only 3.1%, to $1,827M. Spending on R&D and sales grew, and stock-based pay of $544M counts in GAAP profit even though Adobe's non-GAAP number ($2,424M) leaves it out.
takeaways.title: Profit is not keeping up with revenue

verdict: Adobe grew revenue 13% to $6.8B and passed 1 billion monthly users, with its AI-first products' recurring revenue up more than 150% — but net profit rose just 3%, squeezed by heavy product and sales spending.
